templates.title: App Window
templates.desc: A macOS-style window that hosts ANY mix of panels: pipeline, table, list, stats, chat, text, terminal, image, contact. Panels are data, not code.

use.when: The speaker is explaining software, a dashboard or a live record: the screen becomes the subject, the speaker drops to a PiP (camera move) or a split rail.
pairs: camera: speaker PiP or split rail
layout:"rail" puts the headline in the free left column
use.avoid: A single quick fact: use glass-card. Needs a landscape speaker PiP: keep the left column for the headline rail.

vars.railNote: Open the record and confirm every field synced.

templates.title: Before / After
templates.desc: Glass-framed comparison: a divider with a glass handle sweeps across, revealing the after image over the before.

use.when: The speaker contrasts the old way with the new result: a cleanup, a redesign, a messy sheet turned into a pipeline. Hold 4-6 s. On full-frame talking head use side left/right with width 800-900.
pairs: camera: speaker PiP while it plays
use.avoid: Images with different aspect ratios (set aspect), or results with no visual difference.

templates.title: Chapter Pill
templates.desc: Progress pill. The schedule is data and state changes are seek-safe.

use.when: Any video with 2+ named sections. Mount once for the whole video; the schedule moves it.

templates.title: Checklist
templates.desc: Recap list that ticks off one item at a time, with a running "N of N" counter.

use.when: The speaker sums up the steps just covered, or lists what to have ready. Set stagger to the speaking pace.
use.avoid: More than 5 items, or new information: it is a recap, not a teaching card.

variables.label: Items (JSON list of strings)
variables.default: ["Add the contact","Send the form","Check the details"]

templates.title: Contact Card
templates.desc: One CRM record with a verified seal and field tiles.

use.when: A single record is the proof: a contact, lead, customer or booking.
use.avoid: Lists of records: use an app-window table or pipeline.

templates.title: Fast-Forward Badge
templates.desc: Glass pill with a pulsing fast-forward glyph and a speed label in tabular figures, shown while footage is sped up.

use.when: Mount for exactly the span where footage is sped up or a long wait is compressed (installs, imports, loading).
pairs: transition blur (out of the sped-up span)
use.avoid: Real-time footage, or spans under ~1.5 s.

variables.label: Duration (s), the length of the sped-up span

templates.title: Glass Card
templates.desc: One idea at a time: eyebrow, headline with an accent word, and 2-3 supporting rows. The default talking-point graphic.

use.when: Introduce a single method, step or concept while the speaker explains it. Hold 2.5-3.5 s.
use.avoid: More than 3 rows, or a live-software walkthrough: use app-window.

footer.label: Bulk Operations
footer.text: Automated tag assignment & smart list sync

templates.title: iMessage Phone
templates.desc: iPhone 16 Pro iMessage thread with typing indicator.

use.when: The story is a text conversation: an auto-reply, an SMS follow-up, a booking exchange.
pairs: glass-card with aside (phone beside a card)
use.avoid: Email or chat apps; use an app-window chat panel.

variables.label: Thread (JSON)
variables.default: [{"from":"them","text":"New lead: Jane Doe (Opt-in Form)","at":0.8},{"from":"me","text":"AI qualified & booked for 2 PM!","at":1.6}]

templates.title: Keyboard Shortcut
templates.desc: Keycaps that pop in and press as a chord, with an optional caption. Shows what was pressed when the viewer cannot see the keyboard.

use.when: The speaker presses or names a shortcut. Show it the moment it is pressed, hold 2-3 s.
pairs: app-window / screen share (the result of the shortcut)
use.avoid: Long sequences of shortcuts back to back; one per beat.

templates.title: Kinetic Subtitles
templates.desc: Word-by-word subtitle capsules. Cues are data; *star* the 1-3 punch words.

use.when: Always-on pacing for talking-head video. Highlight numbers, verbs and the thesis, never whole sentences.
pairs: any card (keep captions at the bottom, cards at the sides)
use.avoid: Hiding captions behind a PiP; cut a cue when a graphic already shows the same words.

variables.label: Cues [{start,end,text}] - wrap punch words in *stars* (JSON)

templates.title: Link Chip
templates.desc: Glass pill with an accent icon, a call to action and a URL. Bouncy entrance, small icon nudge.

use.when: The speaker points the viewer to a resource: description link, download, booking page. 3-5 s.
use.avoid: Long URLs (use a short path) or more than one chip on screen.

templates.title: Lower Third
templates.desc: Speaker name plate with verified seal.

use.when: First 4 s of the video, or whenever a new speaker appears. Once per speaker.
use.avoid: Repeating the same speaker later in the video.

templates.title: Metric Counter
templates.desc: Big tabular number that counts up.

use.when: A number is the point of the sentence: percent, seconds, money, growth.
use.avoid: More than one number at a time; use an app-window stats panel for several.

use.when: An event happens in the story: a lead arrives, a message lands, a payment clears. Drops in with a bouncy spring.
use.avoid: Static facts: it implies something just happened.

variables.label: Badge icon (bolt, bell, money, chat, mail, calendar, sparkle, star, check)

templates.title: Pull Quote
templates.desc: One key line on glass: accent quotation mark, word-by-word reveal, punch words in blue, attribution last.

use.when: The speaker says the line worth remembering (the thesis), or quotes a customer.
use.avoid: More than ~20 words, or more than one quote per minute.

variables.label: Quote - wrap punch words in *stars*
variables.default: Reply in the first five minutes and the *booking* is yours.

templates.title: Spotlight
templates.desc: Dims everything except a target rectangle, with an accent ring.

use.when: Point the viewer at one area of a busy screen or app-window while the speaker names it.
use.avoid: Plain talking-head shots; it needs something to point at.

templates.title: Title Card
templates.desc: Intro: full-frame blurred scrim with a word-by-word title reveal. Outro: an "Up next" card with a thumbnail and call to action.

use.when: Intro on the opening line that names the topic; outro on the sign-off that points to the next video. Hold 3-4 s.
use.avoid: Mid-video section breaks: use transition (chapter). More than one intro per video.

variables.label: Keep clear of the face (outro only; intro is full frame)

templates.title: Transition
templates.desc: Full-frame transition library over a cut: dip, flash, blur, glass-wipe, iris, light-sweep, chapter. The cut sits at at + dur/2; clear at both ends.

use.when: Cover a cut in the footage: put the cut at the midpoint (at + dur/2). dip = calm scene or time change; flash = energetic reveal (sparingly); blur = soft jump cut in the same setup; glass-wipe = moving to a new screen or app, direction = travel; iris = focusing in on a detail or closing a topic; light-sweep = upbeat "next up" or a win; chapter = named section break (set dur 1.4-2 s).
pairs: camera reframe right after the cut
use.avoid: Stacking transitions on every cut (most cuts need none), and more than one flash per video. Never on a mid-sentence jump cut.

variables.label: Duration (s); the cut sits at at + dur/2 (chapter: use 1.6)
Kind (dip | flash | blur | glass-wipe | iris | light-sweep | chapter)

motion.cue: Thesis, punchline, emotional emphasis
motion.motion: Camera punch-in 1.15-1.25x + edge-defocus pulse
motion.how: camera.js move {scale: 1.2}; never hold a tight punch-in more than 5 s without a reframe

motion.cue: Explaining software, metrics or a diagram
motion.motion: Speaker PiP, 16:9, on the page margin
motion.how: camera.js move {win, fit:"frame", front:true} or __hfGlass.dockPiP; pair with app-window layout:"rail"

motion.cue: Long UI walkthrough or a portrait speaker
motion.motion: Split-stage rail (speaker left, app right)
motion.how: __hfGlass.splitStage: face-centred portrait crop, no re-crop while it morphs

motion.cue: Conclusion, summary, call to action
motion.motion: Back to full-bleed + 1.2x punch-in
motion.how: camera.js move {win:"full", scale:1.2}; speaker returns to eye contact

motion.cue: A card or graphic arrives
motion.motion: snappy spring from the side AWAY from the face (0.6 s), exit power2.in 0.35 s
motion.how: __hfGlass.ease.snappy; templates with safe:true place themselves

motion.cue: Something happens (event, alert)
motion.motion: bouncy drop-in, 4.6% overshoot
motion.how: __hfGlass.ease.bouncy via notification-stack / chat bubbles

motion.cue: A number is spoken
motion.motion: Counter roll 1.4 s, smooth, tabular figures
motion.how: metric-counter (or a stats panel)

motion.cue: One word matters
motion.motion: Punch word: blue + scale 1.1, once per cue
motion.how: kinetic-subtitle *word*; 1-3 words per sentence

motion.cue: Look at this part
motion.motion: Spotlight dim 0.55 + accent ring
motion.how: spotlight template over an app-window panel

motion.cue: Next step in a list
motion.motion: Chapter pill advances, new card replaces the old one
motion.how: chapter-pill schedule + glass-card, one card at a time

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: pointing at a control, field or button
motion.motion: Zoom to the target 1.5-1.9x (spring 0.7 s); PiP tucks to 0.7x
motion.how: projects/screen-share/share.js zooms: [{t, x, y, z}]; zoom OUT ({t, z:1}) before the next topic

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: reading small text or a modal
motion.motion: Zoom 2.0-2.5x, hold 2-4 s
motion.how: Only for text too small at 1080p; never hold a tight zoom without cursor activity

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: switching apps or tabs
motion.motion: Back to overview (z:1) first, then the next zoom
motion.how: Avoid chained zoom-to-zoom jumps; a reset in between reads as a cut

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: speaker talks without touching the screen
motion.motion: Overview, PiP at rest size (1.0x)
motion.how: PiP stays bottom-left on the margin; never move it to another corner

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: a zoom holds longer than ~2 s
motion.motion: Slow drift: +3.5% push-in on the same point until the next keyframe
motion.how: share.js drift: true (or { amount, minHold }); a static zoom looks frozen

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: "click this", "this button", "right here"
motion.motion: Callout: accent ring + label pill, locked to the spot through zooms
motion.how: share.js callouts: [{ t, end, x, y, w, h, label, side }] in screen 0-1 coords; usually inside a zoom

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: "look at this section", "notice"
motion.motion: Focus dim: everything except the region darkens to 55%
motion.how: share.js focus: [{ t, end, x, y, w, h, dim }]; softer than a callout, for areas not buttons

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: an email, API key, phone number or client name is visible
motion.motion: Redact: frosted blur (or solid) box that follows every zoom
motion.how: share.js redact: [{ x, y, w, h }] (whole video) or with t/end; run cue-plan to catch spoken ones

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: talking straight to the viewer (intro, opinion, sign-off)
motion.motion: Webcam swap: the card grows to full screen, then back
motion.how: share.js cam: [{ t, mode: 'full' }, { t, mode: 'pip' }]; no re-crop, face stays centred

motion.cue: SCREEN SHARE: dense screen, the card covers content
motion.motion: Hide webcam: card slides down and out, returns on the next topic
motion.how: share.js cam: [{ t, mode: 'hide' }, { t, mode: 'pip' }]

motion.cue: A pause or filler was cut (jump cut)
motion.motion: Jump-cut punch: framing alternates 1.0 / 1.06 at each cut
motion.how: node scripts/auto-trim.mjs <voice file>, then paste its cuts into share.js cuts or camera.js cuts

motion.cue: Section change, new app or screen, a cut that should feel intended
motion.motion: Transition over the cut (cut at the midpoint): blur 0.8 s by default, glass-wipe for a new screen, chapter 1.6 s for a named section
motion.how: transition template, kind = dip | flash | blur | glass-wipe | iris | light-sweep | chapter; z-index 90; most cuts need none

motion.cue: Breath, filler, mid-sentence pause
motion.motion: No motion
motion.how: Never zoom or move graphics mid-breath; trim dead air > 0.4 s instead
